page_data.en:
Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :- 9.12-8 (17)

HAND GRENADE THROWN INTO OFFICE OF "RUSSIAN DAILY N'S"

At 7.45 p.m. yesterday, a motor car suddenly
stopped in front of the office of the "Russian Daily News,"
No.620 Avenue Foch, and an occupant of the car threw a hand
grenade into the premises. The grenade exploded with a loud
noise, frightening people in the vicinity. The car then
drove away at high speed. The affair took place so quickly
that it was impossible to tell the nationality of the thrower
or to take down the licence number of the motor car.
Upon receipt of a report, Chengtu Road
Police Station detailed Chinese and foreign detectives to
make an investigation. None of the employees of the news-
paper or pedestrians were killed or injured. A show
window in front of the newspaper office was broken and the
iron grille was slightly damaged.
It is said that Mr. Chilikin, editor of the
paper, had arrived at the office only a few minutes before
the incident. It is not known whether the affair was an
attempt to assassinate Mr. Chilikin. The Police are
investigating.

— 5/12 9/2
page_data.zh:
《大公报》及其他本地报纸：- 9.12-8 (17)

手榴弹被投掷进《俄罗斯日报》办公室

昨晚7时45分，一辆汽车突然停在福煦路620号《俄罗斯日报》办公室门前，车内一人向屋内投掷了一枚手榴弹。手榴弹发出巨响爆炸，惊吓了附近居民。随后汽车高速驶离。事发过于迅速，无法辨认投掷者的国籍或记下汽车牌照号码。
接到报告后，成都路警察局派遣中外侦探进行调查。报社员工或行人均无伤亡。报社门前的橱窗玻璃破碎，铁栅栏轻微受损。
据悉，该报主编奇利金先生在事发前几分钟刚到达办公室。尚不清楚此事是否为刺杀奇利金先生的未遂行动。警方正在调查。

— 5/12 9/2

page_data.en:
December 10, 1937.

SHANGHAI GODO

THE FOREIGN CONTROLLED AREAS IN SHANGHAI

The attack upon the office
of the Russian newspaper which had been engaged in anti-
Japanese propaganda by an unknown person gives a good
indication of conditions in the Settlement.
The Settlement must no longer
be allowed to be used as a base for the anti-Japanese
activities. The Settlement is no longer surrounded by
the Chinese army; the Japanese army has saved the
Settlement from being over-ridden by the Chinese army.
The same remark applies in
the case of the French Concession which can not be allowed
to be used as a base for the anti-Japanese activities,
despite the theory that it is not an international area.
The foreign controlled areas
in Shanghai are leased from China and are under Chinese
sovereignty. When such areas are encircled by the
Japanese army, the sovereignty of the areas devolves
upon the Japanese army.
The question of "de jure"
should be set aside and the "de facto" situation should
be considered. The Japanese are not disregarding foreign
interests but they must adopt a policy according to
circumstances.

RADICAL RUSSIAN NEWSPAPER BOMBED

A mysterious bombing case
took place the other day at the "Novosti Dnia," a Russian
newspaper owned by Soviet Russia. This newspaper has
been challenging the anti-Communism movement of Russian
emigrants and publishing anti-Japanese articles in order
to win favour of Chinese.
At about 7 p.m. December 8,
a man alighted from a motorcar in front of the "Novosti
Dnia," No. 620 Avenue Haig, on the International Settlement
side, threw a hand grenade at the newspaper office and
escaped in the motorcar. The missile exploded, destroying
a door but fortunately no one was injured. The nationality
of the culprit is not known but according to an eye-witness
he is a foreigner.
Upon receiving a report of
the affair, foreign and Chinese police officers were sent
by Chengtu Road Police Station to the scene to make an
investigation.
Several days ago a bomb was
discovered at the Soviet Club on Yu Yuen Road, while
another bomb was found in the "Exporthleb," a Soviet
firm, in Grosvenor House in the French Concession. It
is believed that there is some connection between these
three cases.
page_data.zh:
1937年12月10日。

上海上帝

上海的外国控制区

一名身份不明者袭击了从事反日宣传的俄文报社办公室，这很好地表明了租界的现状。
绝不能再允许租界被用作反日活动的基地。租界不再被中国军队包围；日本军队使租界免遭中国军队的践踏。
同样的说法也适用于法租界，尽管有理论认为它不是国际区域，但也不能允许其被用作反日活动的基地。
上海的外国控制区是从中国租赁的，处于中国主权之下。当这些区域被日本军队包围时，这些区域的主权归于日本军队。
“法理”问题应搁置一旁，应考虑“事实”情况。日本人并非无视外国利益，但他们必须根据情况采取政策。

激进俄文报社遭炸弹袭击

日前发生了一起神秘的炸弹案件，地点位于苏维埃俄罗斯拥有的俄文报纸《每日新闻》（Novosti Dnia）。该报一直挑战俄罗斯移民的反共运动，并发表反日文章以赢得中国人的好感。
12月8日晚7时许，一名男子在国际租界一侧海格路（Avenue Haig）620号《每日新闻》报社门前下车，向报社办公室投掷了一枚手榴弹，随后乘车逃离。弹药爆炸，炸毁了一扇门，但幸运的是无人受伤。肇事者的国籍不详，但据目击者称其为外国人。
接到此事报告后，成都路警察局派遣中外警员前往现场进行调查。
几天前，在愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）的苏联俱乐部发现了一枚炸弹，而在法租界格罗斯文纳大楼（Grosvenor House）的苏联公司“出口面包公司”（Exporthleb）也发现了另一枚炸弹。人们相信这三起案件之间存在某种联系。

December 10, 1937.

So far, no person has been
arrested. From an examination of the two hundred pieces
of the hand grenade it is believed that the missile was
home-made. The damage done by the explosion is estimated
at about $300.

Mr. Chilikin, the editor in
chief, who was absent at the time of the explosion, told
a reporter of the "Evening Post" that the culprit is
probably some political lawless element. Prior to the
incident Mr. Chilikin had received threatening letters
and telephone messages. Neither the publication nor the
policy of the newspaper will be altered because of the
incident.

ITINERARY OF THE FLAG PROCESSION ALTERED

The Japanese community here
is awaiting word of the fall of Nanking in order to hold
a big flag procession to mark the historical event.
The sponsor of the procession
has made a few changes in the itinerary which is now as
follows :-

1 p.m. Meet at the former
church site off Woosung Road.

1.15 p.m. Start of the
procession by way of Woosung Road, Kashing Road, North
Szechuen Road, Naval Landing Party Headquarters, worship
at the Shanghai Jinsha Shrine after which back to North
Szechuen Road, Range Road, North Haining Road, Woosung
Road, Haining Road, Chapoo Road, Boone Road, Seward Road,
Broadway, Fearon Road, the Flagship "Idzumo," Japanese
Consulate, North Soochow Road, Woosung Road, finishing
at the church site.

JAPANESE CONSULATE COMPILING RECORD OF DAMAGE DONE BY
HOSTILITIES

The Japanese Consulate
announces that an investigation will be made into the
damage caused by the present hostilities. This enquiry
will be used as the fundamental and official record of
the damage. Those who have failed to register their
cases should apply to the enquiry office.

MEETING OF CORPORATION'S REHABILITATION COMMITTEE

The Rehabilitation Committee
of the Japanese Residents' Corporation held a meeting
yesterday at the Corporation's office on Quinsan Road
and discussed the question of the restoration of the
gas, water and electricity supplies.

1937年12月10日。

截至目前，尚未逮捕任何人。通过对两百块手榴弹碎片的检查，认为该弹药是自制武器。爆炸造成的损失估计约为300美元。

总编辑奇利金先生在爆炸发生时不在场，他告诉《晚邮报》记者，肇事者可能是某些政治不法之徒。在事件发生前，奇利金先生曾收到威胁信和电话留言。此次事件不会改变报纸的出版或其政策。

旗帜游行路线变更

此地的日本侨民社区正等待南京陷落的消息，以便举行大型旗帜游行来纪念这一历史事件。
游行主办方对路线进行了一些更改，现路线如下：-

下午1点 在吴淞路旁的原教堂遗址集合。

下午1点15分 游行开始，途经吴淞路、嘉兴路、四川北路、海军陆战队总部，在上海金刀神社参拜后返回四川北路、靶子路、海宁北路、吴淞路、海宁路、乍浦路、百老汇路（Boone Road）、熙华德路（Seward Road）、百老汇路（Broadway）、斐伦路（Fearon Road）、旗舰“出云”号、日本领事馆、苏州河北路、吴淞路，最后回到教堂遗址。

日本领事馆编制战事损失记录

日本领事馆宣布，将对当前战事造成的损失进行调查。此次调查将作为损失的基础和官方记录。那些尚未登记案件的人应向调查办公室申请。

公司复兴委员会会议

日本居留民团复兴委员会昨日在昆山路的公司办公室举行会议，讨论了恢复煤气、供水和电力供应的问题。

Sin Wan Pao of Dec.9:

"HAND GRENADE LANDED AT DOOR OF RUSSIAN NEWSPAPER"

At 7.45 p.m. yesterday a hand grenade landed
at the entrance to the "Russian Daily News" (俄文日報),
No.620 Avenue Foch, and when it exploded, the show window
was smashed to pieces.

Fortunately, no one was wounded. After the
incident, the management of the newspaper made a report
to the Police Station. The Police are investigating.

"RUFFIAN THROWS BOMB IN FRONT OF RUSSIAN NEWSPAPER
OFFICE"

At 7.45 p.m. yesterday a ruffian threw a
bomb at the office of the "Russian Daily News," No.620
Avenue Foch. It exploded immediately, breaking a
large pane of glass. The thrower made good his
escape.

-------------

Eastern Times of Dec.9:

"BOMB THROWN IN FRONT OF THE 'RUSSIAN DAILY NEWS'"

At 7.45 p.m. yesterday a bomb was thrown at
the office of the "Russian Daily News," No.620 Avenue
Foch. The bomb exploded outside the office, breaking
a large pane of glass in front of the building but
injuring nobody.

Upon receipt of a report, Chinese and foreign
detectives and policemen went to make enquiries but the
bomb-thrower had already escaped. The Police are
making an investigation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition published the following
article on December 9 :-

EXPLOSION OF A HAND GRENADE IN FRONT OF THE "RUSSIAN DAILY
NEWS"

Window Panes Shattered But Nobody Injured
Motive Being Investigated

At 7.45 p.m. yesterday a hand grenade was
thrown by some person in front of the "Russian Daily
News" at 620 Avenue Foch. The heavy explosion shattered
the large window panes of the office. The thrower made
good his escape.

After the incident, a report was immediately
made to the Police by a responsible official of the paper.
The damage done to the window panes of the newspaper
office is estimated at $500. Fortunately no one was
injured. Nothing is known as to the cause of the attack.

主题：1937年12月6日霞飞路620号炸弹爆炸案——关于“全俄民族革命法西斯党”的调查。

制作人：M.S.I. Prokofiev    转呈人：C Gasson [签名]

N. Svetloff 和 A. Makeyeff 在联合声明中提到的政治组织，是所谓的“全俄民族革命法西斯党”的地方分支，其领导人是某位 A.A. Vonsiatsky，此人为俄裔归化美国公民，居住在美国康涅狄格州普特南（Putnam, Conn.）。据报道，他的妻子是一位富有的美国人的女儿，拥有巨额资产（如果相信报刊报道的话，达10,000,000美元），这一事实构成了 Vonsiatsky 政治活动的财政基础。自1936年3月他访问上海以来，当地的小组或其支持者一直收到足以出版其名为《俄罗斯先锋报》（Russian Vanguard）的小型周报以及维持其俱乐部运营的津贴。目前，《俄罗斯先锋报》的编辑部及俱乐部位于华琪路96号、贝当路1025号，而该报的印刷厂则占用华琪路63号附属的一个车库。

该小组负责人 K.A. Stekloff 是前俄国军队的一名低级战时军官，目前受雇于一名居住在威海卫路647号50室的中国人，担任其保镖。从已知的 Stekloff 的背景以及与此人的个人接触来看，他似乎缺乏人们期望政治领袖所具备的足够教育和经验。这解释了《俄罗斯先锋报》的低水准，也可能解释了 Stekloff 明显倾向于从事纯粹表面性质的活动，例如：展示法西斯制服和带有党徽（卐字标志）的徽章，为成员引入宣誓仪式，组建“突击组”、“方阵”，印制反共传单，名义上是为了寄送

them to the U.S.S.R. etc. All this appears to be calculated to
make a show of activities and thus to justify the subsidy receiv-
ed from Vonsiatsky. There are good reasons to believe that Stekloff
is personally interested in the subsidy and it was frequently re-
ported that there were controversies over this matter between him
and his followers.

No secret whatever has been made of the existence
of the "storm group" within this organization and it was mentio-
ned in the "Russian Vanguard" that a certain M.Ya.Rojnovsky is
its "chief". Although the functions of the "storm group" are not
quite clear, there is no evidence that it is a "terrorist organi-
zation" as is alleged by Svetloff and Makeyeff and as its name
may suggest. Stekloff explained that members of both sexes who have
passed a period of probation and have taken the prescribed "oath"
are admitted into the "storm group" which at present is about 40
strong. The higher gradation in membership is the "phalanx" to
which only 4-5 leading members belong. The bulk of the Stekloff
group consists of former members of the Russian Detachment in
Marshal Chang Chung Chang's army in Shantung, in which Stekloff
served for a couple of years.

In March, 1935 Stekloff came to the notice of the Mu-
nicipal Police in connection with a confidential despatch from
the Public Safety Bureau to the effect that, according to Soviet
sources, his group was "plotting to assassinate the Soviet Ambas-
sador". Police enquiries into this matter did not elicit any in-
formation which could substantiate this allegation. The origin of
the allegation was probably due to idle gossip among individual
members of this and other political groups, a coloured version of
which might have been reported to the Soviet authorities by

该组织内存在“突击组”一事并非秘密，《俄罗斯先锋报》曾提及某位 M.Ya. Rojnovsky 是其“首领”。虽然“突击组”的职能尚不完全清楚，但没有证据表明它是 Svetloff 和 Makeyeff 所声称的、且如其名称可能暗示的“恐怖组织”。Stekloff 解释说，男女成员在经过一段试用期并按规定进行“宣誓”后，方可加入“突击组”，目前该组约有40人。成员中的更高级别是“方阵”，只有4-5名核心成员属于此列。Stekloff 小组的大部分成员由前张宗昌元帅在山东军队中的俄罗斯分队成员组成，Stekloff 曾在其中服役两年。

1935年3月，Stekloff 因公共安全局发来的一份机密函件而引起工部局警务处的注意，该函件称，据苏联方面消息，他的小组正“策划刺杀苏联大使”。警方对此事的调查未能获取任何能证实这一指控的信息。该指控的来源可能是由于该政治团体及其他政治团体的个别成员之间的无聊闲谈，经过添油加醋的版本可能被

On December 13 in connection with the registration
of the club established by Stekloff at 96 Hwa Kee Avenue, the un-
dersigned had an opportunity of examining a list of former and
present members of his group and noticed the name of N.M. Ermola-
yeff with a red ink mark against it. Stekloff stated that Ermo-
layeff joined the group in 1936, but that he had shown very
little interest in its activities and since May, 1937 had not at-
tended lectures and other functions at the club. Asked regard-
ing the significance, if any, of the red ink mark referred to
above Stekloff explained that he had marked Ermolayeff's name
for an investigation into his antecedents and activities, as he
was suspected of being a Soviet agent. While it is true that
Stekloff is apt to brand as bolsheviks many of his former mem-
bers, especially those who questioned his right of the uncontrol-
led handling of Vonsiatsky's subsidy, it appears from the above
that Ermolayeff is not likely to be one of the "storm group" in-
to which only "reliable" members are admitted. This makes very
doubtful the possibility of Mojnovsky and Ermolayeff's joint par-
ticipation in the bombing affair in question.

12月13日，就 Stekloff 在华琪路96号建立的俱乐部的注册事宜，签署人有机会查阅了他小组的前成员和现成员名单，并注意到 N.M. Ermolayeff 的名字旁有一个红墨水标记。Stekloff 称，Ermolayeff 于1936年加入该小组，但他对其活动兴趣甚微，自1937年5月以来未参加俱乐部的讲座和其他活动。当被问及上述红墨水标记是否有何意义时，Stekloff 解释说，他标记 Ermolayeff 的名字是为了调查其背景和活动，因为怀疑他是苏联代理人。虽然 Stekloff 确实倾向于将许多前成员，特别是那些质疑他无权随意支配 Vonsiatsky 津贴的人，贴上布尔什维克的标签，但从上述情况来看，Ermolayeff 不太可能是只接纳“可靠”成员的“突击组”的一员。这使得 Mojnovsky 和 Ermolayeff 共同参与此次炸弹爆炸案的可能性非常值得怀疑。

mous hangman" for his past activities in a White Russian detach-
ment in Mongolia. Makeyeff was also the subject of very uncom-

the pro-Soviet "Repatriation Union". Hence Makeyeff's com-

being assaulted by his enemies.

    It is of interest to note that Vdovin implicating in
his statement Ermolayeff does not mention the name of the parti-
cular political group to which the latter individual belongs.
The allegations against the Stekloff group are only a guess
work on the part of Svetloff and Makeyeff, President and Secre-

a member of the same Union.

    In view of the foregoing it appears that there is no
tangible evidence to connect the Stekloff group with the explo-
sion at 620 Avenue Joffre.

    It is possible that Ermolayeff belongs to some other
group of local Russians who are hostile to Chilikin and to the
"Repatriation Union" with which his newspaper is closely con-
nected. Enquiries in this direction are proceeding.

鉴于上述情况，似乎没有确凿证据将 Stekloff 小组与霞飞路620号的爆炸案联系起来。

Ermolayeff 可能属于当地其他敌视 Chilikin 及其报纸密切相关的“归国联盟”的俄罗斯人团体。这方面的调查正在进行中。

Translation from Russian.

Statement for the Police - secret

Andrey Mihailovich VOLK, 32 Russian emigrant residing at
682 Rue Bourget, House 9. Unemployed.

At about 9 p.m. on November 20, 1937, I met N.N.
Ermolaieff on route des Soeurs near Avenue Joffre. He started
a conversation with me as with an acquaintance of his. He
asked what I was doing and how I did get the means of
livelihood.

"You are, probably, very hard up?" said he and then
asked if I visited the Soviet Consulate. If I did, said
he, it was to no purpose. - "You better stick to the emi-
grants", continued he: "Life in the U.S.S.R. is very hard
and anyhow, you won't be able to return to Russia."

I replied that I had already been an emigrant for
a long time. How else could I stick to them?

"This is not the point" said he, "You do not under-
stand me. You should join some organization."

I said that I do not recognize any organizations
and that my aim is to return to my homeland.

"You must believe me," said he, "we have an organi-
zation."

"The Fascists?"

"No" said he: "Another organization, but at present
I will not tell you its name. This organization can put
you on a watchman's job, and anyhow you will be in employ-
ment."

He insisted that I should join their organization
and that if I wished to do so, he could say a word for me.
I refused.

"But think it over," said he, "I can arrange for
the necessary introductions."

He then began to talk frankly:
page_data.zh:
俄语译文。

致警方的陈述 - 机密

Andrey Mihailovich VOLK，32岁，俄罗斯侨民，居住于勃艮第路682号9室。无业。

1937年11月20日晚9时许，我在靠近霞飞路的修女路（route des Soeurs）遇到了 N.N. Ermolaieff。他像熟人一样与我攀谈起来。他问我在做什么，以及如何维持生计。

“你可能很缺钱吧？”他说，然后问我是否去过苏联领事馆。如果去过，他说，那是徒劳的。“你最好还是依附于侨民圈子，”他继续说道：“苏联的生活非常艰难，而且无论如何，你也无法返回俄罗斯。”

我回答说，我已经是侨民很久了。不然我怎么依附他们呢？

“问题不在这里，”他说，“你不明白我的意思。你应该加入某个组织。”

我说我不承认任何组织，我的目标是回到祖国。

“你必须相信我，”他说，“我们有一个组织。”

“法西斯分子？”

“不，”他说：“是另一个组织，但我现在不会告诉你它的名字。这个组织可以给你安排一份看守的工作，总之你会有一份工作。”

他坚持要我加入他们的组织，并表示如果我愿意，他可以为我引荐。我拒绝了。

“再考虑一下，”他说，“我可以安排必要的介绍。”

随后他开始坦率地谈论：

page_data.en:
- 2 -

"I know you," said he, "and you must not tell
anybody about our conversation. Only you alone should
know about it. But if you tell anybody about it, you
will be in trouble."

He went on to tell me that he could undertake
the task of throwing bombs into Soviet institutions,
including the "Novost Dnia." He said that he either
would send me to place the explosives at the Soviet
institutions or would do this together with me.

As I knew from his own statements that he had
fled from the U.S.S.R., I began to dissuade him from
carrying out this plan. I said that he should be
ashamed to act against the Soviet Government in whose
service he was formerly.

Among other things he said that he is a qualified
pyrotechnician and that there is no other such specialist
here.

When we were parting he repeated that I should
keep our conversation secret.

Our next meeting was at about 5 p.m. on December
9, at the corner of Avenue Joffre and Route des Soeurs.
On seeing me he approached me and said:

"You see, I only was joking when we had that
conversation, but the joke has come true."

I replied that the occurrence was to be very much
regretted.

"Well, I must go," said he, and went away.

I have only a slight acquaintance of Ermolayeff.

Signed: A.M. Vdovin
10.12.37
Shanghai.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

“我认识你，”他说，“你不得向任何人透露我们的谈话内容。只有你一个人可以知道这件事。但如果你告诉任何人，你会有麻烦的。”

他接着告诉我，他可以承担向苏联机构投掷炸弹的任务，包括针对《今日新闻》（Novost Dnia）。他说，他要么派我去苏联机构放置炸药，要么与我一同前往执行。

鉴于我从他的自述中得知他是从苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟（U.S.S.R.）逃出来的，我便开始劝他不要实施这一计划。我说，他曾经为苏联政府效力，现在却采取反对行动，应当感到羞耻。

他还提到，他是一名合格的烟火技师，而且这里没有其他此类专家。

我们分别时，他再次强调我要对谈话内容保密。

我们下一次见面是在12月9日下午5点左右，地点在霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）与修女路（Route des Soeurs）的拐角处。他一见到我就走近我说：

“你看，上次谈话时我只是在开玩笑，但这个玩笑成真了。”

我回答说，发生这种事非常令人遗憾。

“好吧，我得走了，”他说完便离开了。

我与叶尔莫拉耶夫（Ermolayeff）仅有一面之缘。

签名：A.M. 弗多温（Vdovin）

上海。

Regarding the remarks of the D.D.O. "A" Div., the Indian Watchman Babu Singh, employed by the Continental Motors, opposite the scene of this offence, was again interrogated but states that he observed no "tall" person in the vicinity following the bomb exploding.

The above watchman saw a motor car, number unknown, stop east of the scene immediately after the explosion, but this again proceeded upon its journey and no passenger alighted.

This would indicate that the motorists heard the explosion, stopped their car, but ascertaining that it had nothing to do with their vehicle, also observing nothing unusual, proceeded on their way.

The above persons made written statements concern-
ing their knowledge of the offence, and suspicions
regarding those responsible, these now being attached
to file, but the statements made and information gained
is of doubtful value, appearing to be based mostly upon
hearsay and personal animosity, also having the face
appearance of being prepared beforehand by the complain-
ant with whom two of the witnesses are employed, and
with whom, all are closely connected and most probably
in the same clique.

It would also appear strange that this information
was unavailable at the time of initial investigation,
at which time V. Chilikin appeared averse to giving
information, yet the following day he is able to produce
three witnesses, one of whom can state that two suspi-
cious male Russians were in the near vicinity at the
time of the offence, whilst the other two witnesses are
able, or desire to give, the names of two identical
persons, whom they state are actively engaged in propa-
ganda and intimidation, yet strangely enough are members
of a different political group.

The source of this information also its value
appears to be questionable, when the evidence of N.A.
Schegoleff, who was standing outside the premises at

上述人员就其对案情的了解以及对责任人的怀疑提交了书面陈述，现附于卷宗。但这些陈述及所获信息的价值存疑，似乎主要基于道听途说和个人恩怨，并且表面上看来是由控告人预先准备好的，两名证人受雇于该控告人，且所有证人都与其关系密切，很可能属于同一派系。

此外，奇怪的是，这些信息在初步调查时无法获得，当时V. 奇利金似乎不愿提供信息，然而第二天他却能引出三名证人，其中一人声称在案发时附近有两名可疑的俄罗斯男子，而另外两名证人则能够或愿意指出两名相同人员的姓名，称他们积极参与宣传和恐吓活动，但奇怪的是，这些人属于不同的政治团体。

当考虑到站在 premises 外的N.A. 谢戈列夫（Schegoleff）的证词时，这一信息来源及其价值似乎也值得怀疑，他在

    尽管来自室内的光线使得建筑物外部的照明相当良好，但在与该被点名的人交谈后，证人“认为”自己无法进行指认，然而其他证人却试图根据极为简略的描述，明确牵连已知人员。
    同时，考虑到这些人在一个政治党派中的地位，而该党派的观点与其雇主的观点相左，推测L.A. 赫鲁林斯基夫人认识这些人是合理的。如果这一推测正确，那么这位女士正在暗示一条调查线索，而其他证人的怀疑部分佐证了这条线索，所有这些证人都是代表V. 奇利金并在其唆使下行事，其目的不为调查人员所知。

    据称，前者是制造炸弹的专家，虽无业但资金充裕；后者是当地一个由名为“A. 冯西亚茨基”（A. Vonsiatsky）的人领导的“法西斯党”分支中的“风暴分队队长”，该领导人居住在美国康涅狄格州汤普森（Thompson, Connecticut, U.S.A.）。
    就本报告所述的轰炸罪行而言，后者及其法西斯党在本地的重要性较为模糊，但据推测源于该党的全球分支网络，该党旨在恢复沙皇制度以取代现有的苏联政府。控告人提供的美国报纸剪报据称证明了这一点，这些剪报提及在该党领袖家中举行的一次大会，届时“已故沙皇的侄子、英国国王乔治六世陛下的远房堂兄弟费奥多尔亲王殿下”将出席。
    在出席之前的一次记者招待会上，A. 冯西亚茨基谈到该党决心通过宣传而非武力拥立合法的统治者。

several local Russian organisations.

    Regarding the statements of the male witnesses,
the same clique is again evident, not only this, the
same party and supposition, and several points in their
statement are at variance with logic and sane reasoning

    Why a stranger and non-member of a revolutionist
party should be approached to place a bomb in the
Consulate of the U.S.S.R., instead of a bona-fide member
of the revolutionary party is hard to comprehend, and
granting that this was done, no connection with the
bombing of the Soviet firm "Exporthleb," nor that of the
"Soviet Club" has yet been proved.

    This aspect of the case and probable connection is
now under investigation.

    Upon his own admission, the witness Maketoff is not
on good terms with the persons he attempts to implicate;
and as previously stated, this attempted implication
upon the rather vague statement of Mrs. Krulinsky is
unsubstantiated by investigations made at the scene
immediately following the incident.

    关于男性证人的陈述，同样的派系痕迹再次显现，不仅如此，还表现出相同的党派立场和推测，且他们陈述中的几点与逻辑和理性推理相悖。

    为何要接触一个革命政党的局外人和非成员，让其去苏联领事馆放置炸弹，而不是由该革命政党的正式成员执行，这令人难以理解。即便假设此事属实，目前也尚未证明这与轰炸苏联企业“出口粮食公司”（Exporthleb）或“苏联俱乐部”（Soviet Club）有任何关联。

    案件的这一方面及可能的联系目前正在调查中。

    根据证人马凯托夫（Maketoff）自己的承认，他与他试图牵连的人关系不和；如前所述，这种基于赫鲁林斯基（Krulinsky）夫人相当模糊的陈述而进行的牵连企图，并未得到事发后立即在现场进行的调查的证实。

        考虑到控告人的政治声誉及其与证人的密切关系，对方表现出的不信任很可能是有道理的。一个据称组织严密的恐怖团伙的领导人，竟然醉到向其预定受害者透露该团伙高层刺杀他的计划，这听起来荒诞不经。
        关于所提供的美国报纸剪报，这些似乎都来自A. 冯西亚茨基住所附近的当地媒体，未见大型美国报刊参与报道。
        显然，在前俄国皇室成员参加的白俄大会上，在美国农村地区会引起当地媒体的大量评论，但在美国举行会议与上海一家声誉可疑、由已知具有共产主义倾向且反感白俄势力的人经营的俄罗斯报纸被炸之间，似乎不能赋予任何特殊的意义。

page_data.en:
Translation from Russian

At about 8 p.m. December 8, 1937, I. Lydia
Alexeyevna HRULINSKY, residing at 60 Rue Paul Henry and
employed as a translator in the editorial offices of the
newspaper "NOVOSTI DNIA", 620 Avenue Foch, while descend-
ing the stairs at the office, heard a loud explosion on
the ground floor of the premises. Descending quickly
and coming out of the premises, I noticed near the
entrance a Russian, about 30 years of age, middle height,
clean-shaven, wearing brown overcoat, black cap and
black boots. On seeing me he made a few steps aside,
but then came up to me and said: "We were passing by
and suddenly we heard an explosion. What has happened?"
I replied that apparently a bomb or a grenade had been
thrown into our offices. Near the tree was standing
another male, tall, wearing dark-grey drap over-coat
and dark-grey panama hat. He shouted to the individual
who was talking to me: "Come on, let us go. Why should
we stand here." They then proceeded in the direction
of the Yates Road.

Lydia Alexeyevna Hrulinsky

December 9, 1937
Shanghai.

I had only a casual glance at the two Russians and
I don't think that I could identify them if I saw them
again.

L. Hrulinsky
page_data.zh:
俄语译文

1937年12月8日晚8时许，我，Lydia Alexeyevna HRULINSKY，居住于亨利路60号，受雇于霞飞路620号《NOVOSTI DNIA》报社编辑部担任翻译，在办公室下楼时，听到楼下传来一声巨大的爆炸声。我迅速下楼并走出大楼，注意到入口附近有一名俄罗斯人，约30岁，中等身材，面部光洁无胡须，身穿棕色大衣，头戴黑色帽子，脚穿黑色靴子。他看到我后向旁边走了几步，但随后又走上前来对我说：“我们路过时突然听到一声爆炸。发生了什么事？”我回答说，似乎有人向我们的办公室投掷了炸弹或手榴弹。树旁还站着另一名男子，身材高大，身穿深灰色呢子大衣，头戴深灰色巴拿马帽。他对正在与我交谈的那个人喊道：“走吧，我们走。我们站在这里干什么。”随后他们朝 Yates Road（音译）方向走去。

Lydia Alexeyevna Hrulinsky

1937年12月9日
上海。

我只是偶然瞥了那两名俄罗斯人一眼，我想如果再次见到他们，我也无法认出他们。

L. Hrulinsky

page_data.en:
Translation from Russian.

WITNESSES:

Alexander Semenovich MAKEYEFF, 40, Russian emigrant,
residing at House 1, Room 3, Hwa Kee Avenue, Tel. 33465.
Unemployed. Has been residing in Shanghai since Octo-
ber 5, 1936.

Nikolay Fedorovich SVETLOFF, 38, Russian emigrant, Jour-
nalist residing at 569 Avenue du Roi Albert, Apt. 23-A.
Has been residing in Shanghai since 1931.

On December 1 we, the undersigned, met on the street
Mr. VDOVIN who is our good friend. He told us that a few days
ago he had met one Nikolay Nikolayevich ERMOLAYEFF. The latter
approached him in a friendly manner and started a conversation.
During the course of the conversation he offered Vdovin to work
together with him in a secret fascist organization the name of
which he did not disclose.

- You live in need, said he, and we have money, can rent a
room for you and help you. You will have little to do in return.
You have been visiting the Soviet Consulate and Soviet institu-
tions. Your task will be to bring in secretly a small box and
leave it somewhere in a corner.

In order to get more information Vdovin pretended that
he was agreeable to the scheme and said that the offer was not
so bad and that he was fed up of living in need.

-Well then, think it over - said Ermolayeff- and we will
meet again and discuss the matter in detail.

After this they parted.

Two days afterwards an explosion took place at the premis-
es of the Soviet firm EXPORTHLEB. The character of the explosion
reminded of the scheme which was the subject of the above conver-
sation. As is known, a home made bomb in the shape of a box ex-
ploded at that address and prior to this another cracker of a si-
milar type exploded at the Soviet Club.

Vdovin knows Ermolayeff and told us that the latter is
a pyrotechnician by profession and claims to be able to make in-

俄语译文。

证人：

Alexander Semenovich MAKEYEFF，40岁，俄裔移民，居住于华琪路1号3室，电话 33465。失业。自1936年10月5日起居住在上海。

Nikolay Fedorovich SVETLOFF，38岁，俄裔移民，记者，居住于阿尔伯特王路569号23-A室。自1931年起居住在上海。

12月1日，我们具名人在街上遇到了我们的好友 VDOVIN 先生。他告诉我们，几天前他遇到了一位名叫 Nikolay Nikolayevich ERMOLAYEFF 的人。后者友好地接近他并开始交谈。在谈话过程中，他邀请 Vdovin 与他一起在一个秘密的法西斯组织中工作，但他并未透露该组织的名称。

“你生活困苦，”他说，“而我们有资金，可以为你租一个房间并提供帮助。作为回报，你需要做的事情很少。你曾访问过苏联领事馆和苏联机构。你的任务是将一个小箱子秘密带入，并将其留在某个角落。”

为了获取更多信息，Vdovin 假装同意该计划，并表示这个提议还不错，他也厌倦了贫困的生活。

“那么，好好考虑一下，” Ermolayeff 说，“我们会再见面，详细讨论此事。”

随后他们分开了。

两天后，苏联公司 EXPORTHLEB（出口粮食公司）的办公地点发生了一起爆炸事件。爆炸的性质让人想起上述谈话中提到的计划。众所周知，在该地址发生了一枚箱形自制炸弹的爆炸，在此之前，另一枚类似类型的爆竹在苏联俱乐部爆炸。

Vdovin 认识 Ermolayeff，并告诉我们后者是一名职业烟火技师，声称能够制造恐

page_data.en:
-2-

Terrorist machines.

According to our information, Ermolayeff is unemployed.
However, he manages to exist and spends money freely. Further-
more, he is a member of A. VONSIATSKY's Fascist party which has
a branch here with V. SHELOFF at the head, who resides at 90
Hwa Kee Avenue. As is known, A. Vonsiatsky's party has already
been exposed in connection with a series of terrorist acts in
America and in connection with keeping arms, on which subject
much was written in American newspapers. We have no doubt that
the local branch is engaged in similar activities. In proof of
this we attach to this statement a series of newspaper cuttings
from American newspapers on the subject.

As is known to us, a certain Lil. ROJNOVSKY is the
"Chief of Storm Detachment" in the local branch of A. Vonsiatsky's
party. The tasks of this detachment include the carrying out ter-
rorist acts against Soviet and pro-Soviet institutions and in-
dividuals.

As there are witnesses who state that they saw two in-
dividuals near the scene of the explosion - one tall and one of
medium height- we think that the individuals in question were:
the one of medium height- ERMOLAYEFF and the tall one- ROJNOV-
SKY.

Witness A. Makeyeff has known Ermolayeff from December,
1936, when the latter lived at 22 Linda Terrace in a room adjoin-
ing his. At that time Makeyeff's attention was attracted by the
fact that Ermolayeff constantly watched him and also because **〔此处转录不清〕**
Ermolayeff asked one Vladimir GODLEVSKY, a friend of Makeyeff,
to furnish information as to who visited Makeyeff, how he got
the money for living expenses etc. Being indignant of this re-
quest Godlevsky told about it to Makeyeff, after which the lat-
ter forbade Ermolayeff to come to his room.

Regarding Rojnovsky Makeyeff knows the following:-

Several months ago Makeyeff met Rojnovsky on Avenue
Joffre. During the course of a conversation Rojnovsky, who was
under the influence of drink, said that he, in his capacity of
page_data.zh:
-2-

怖装置。

根据我们要掌握的信息，Ermolayeff 处于失业状态。然而，他得以维持生计并挥霍金钱。此外，他是 A. VONSIATSKY 法西斯党的成员，该党在此地设有分支，由居住在华琪路90号的 V. SHELOFF 领导。众所周知，A. Vonsiatsky 的政党已因在美国涉及一系列恐怖活动以及持有武器而被揭露，美国报纸对此进行了大量报道。我们毫无疑问，当地分支机构也在从事类似活动。为此，我们在本供词后附上了一系列关于此主题的美国报纸剪报作为证明。

据我们所知，某位 Lil. ROJNOVSKY 是 A. Vonsiatsky 政党当地分支的“冲锋队队长”。该分队的任务包括对苏联及亲苏机构和人员实施恐怖行为。

由于有证人称他们在爆炸现场附近看到两个人——一个高个子，一个中等身材——我们认为相关人员是：中等身材者为 ERMOLAYEFF，高个子者为 ROJNOVSKY。

证人 A. Makeyeff 自1936年12月起认识 Ermolayeff，当时后者居住在 Linda Terrace（音译）22号，房间紧邻 Makeyeff 的房间。当时，Makeyeff 注意到 Ermolayeff 经常监视他，此外 **〔此处转录不清〕** Ermolayeff 请求 Makeyeff 的朋友 Vladimir GODLEVSKY 提供有关谁拜访过 Makeyeff、他如何获得生活费等信息。Godlevsky 对这一请求感到愤慨，并将此事告知了 Makeyeff，此后 Makeyeff 禁止 Ermolayeff 进入他的房间。

关于 Rojnovsky，Makeyeff 知道以下情况：

几个月前，Makeyeff 在霞飞路遇到了 Rojnovsky。在谈话过程中，受酒精影响的 Rojnovsky 表示，他作为冲

page_data.en:
-3-

the Chief of Storm Detachment, had been ordered to kill Makeyeff,
but thatknowing the latter from childhood, and pity for him
and, therefore, detailed for the carrying out of the order in
question members who possessed little energy and were afraid
to carry out the order . The order was given by K.A.Stekloff,
head of the local branch of Vonsiatsky's party.

We are firmly convinced that all terrorist plans ori-
ginate in this group and, acting solely on instinct of self-pre-
servation, we deem it necessary to report this matter to the Po-
lice.

Witness Makeyeff is persecuted by the Fascist party
because during the course of the last year he made a trip to the
U.S.S.R. and now is marked by white organizations as a dangerous
political enemy. He also is the secretary of the Repatriation
Union at Shanghai.

Signed: N.Svetloff
A.Makeyeff.
page_data.zh:
-3-

锋队队长，曾接到命令要杀死 Makeyeff，但由于从小认识后者，并对他怀有怜悯之情，因此指派了一些缺乏精力且不敢执行该命令的成员去执行此项命令。该命令由 Vonsiatsky 政党当地分支负责人 K.A. Stekloff 下达。

我们坚信所有恐怖计划均源于该团伙，出于单纯的自我保护本能，我们认为有必要将此事项报告警方。

证人 Makeyeff 受到法西斯党的迫害，因为他在过去一年中曾前往苏联旅行，现在被白色组织标记为危险的政治敌人。他也是上海归国联盟的秘书。

签名：N. Svetloff
A. Makeyeff。

page_data.en:
At 7.50 p.m. on the 2/12/37, a telephone
message was received from the Russian Daily News,
stating that a bomb had been thrown into the above
premises, situated at 620 Avenue Foch.

The undersigned, D.S.I. Tsai Liu, Sub-Inspector
Alazzin and C.D.C. 198 conducted enquiries at the
scene of offence and there ascertained the following
information.

Scene of Offence are the premises occupied
by the above news journal, operated by a Russian
named V. Chilikin, known to be strongly inclined
toward Communistic tendencies.

At about 7.45 p.m. on the 2/12/37, the ground
floor of the premises were occupied by three employ-
ees, these being engaged in setting up printing type
and named as under:-

1/ Teang Yeong Te (張榮廷) Type-setter.
2/ Tsai Chien Te (蔡錢氏) " "
3/ Kiang Mao Dong (江茂東) " "

At this time, V. Chilikin was engaged with
friends in the upper portion of the premises, and
one of his Russian news reporters named N.A. Scho-
goleff was standing on the pavement at the entrance
of the premises.

The premises are of the shop type, with large
windows, these being protected by iron grilles, and
at the time of the offence, the grille on the east
window was expanded, and that on the west side
window closed and compact.

At 7.45 p.m., a loud detonation occurred, and
page_data.zh:
1937年12月2日晚上7点50分，接到来自《俄罗斯每日新闻》的电话留言，称一枚炸弹被投掷到位于霞飞路620号的上述场所。

具名人 D.S.I. 蔡刘（音译）、副督察 Alazzin 和 C.D.C. 198 在犯罪现场进行了调查，并查明了以下信息。

犯罪现场是上述新闻期刊占用的场所，该期刊由一名名为 V. Chilikin 的俄罗斯人经营，众所周知，他具有强烈的共产主义倾向。

1937年12月2日晚上7点45分左右，该场所的一楼有三名雇员，他们正在从事排版工作，名单如下：-

1/ Teang Yeong Te (張榮廷) 排字工。
2/ Tsai Chien Te (蔡錢氏) " "
3/ Kiang Mao Dong (江茂東) " "

此时，V. Chilikin 正在场所上层与朋友在一起，他的一名俄罗斯新闻记者 N.A. Schogoleff 正站在场所入口处的人行道上。

该场所为店铺类型，拥有大窗户，窗户装有铁栅栏保护，在案发时，东侧窗户的栅栏是展开的，而西侧窗户的栅栏是关闭且紧闭的。

晚上7点45分，发生了一声巨大的爆炸声，并

page_data.en:
1/Sheet No. 3.

this caused the window on the west to be shattered, and
inmates immediately took cover.

Nothing further occurred, and a report was first
made to Police Headquarters and then to this station,
with resultant Police attendance.

Observation at the scene ascertained that the bomb
had not been thrown, but had been placed between the
iron grille and the window on the left side.

The force of explosion had caused the closed grille
to bend outwards and had shattered the window, but no
injury had been caused to inmates or pedestrians on the
roadway, neither to the inside of the premises.

The three employees working inside could give no
information as to the cause of the offence.

The above named newspaper reporter attached to the
staff and standing on the pavement at the time of the
offence, was also unable to supply any information as
to the reason or cause of the offence, but stated that
nothing had taken place on the roadway that would arouse
any suspicion.

However, C.P.V. 975 on duty at the entrance of Lane
632 Avenue Joffre, stated that immediately following the
explosion, he had observed a male Chinese wearing a long
gown, run from the scene, enter an unknown motor car,
which had then driven off in an easterly direction.
page_data.zh:
1/页号 3。

导致西侧窗户破碎，屋内人员立即躲避。

此后未发生其他事情，首先向警察总局报告，然后向本巡捕房报告，警方随即出警。

现场观察确定，炸弹并非被投掷，而是被放置在左侧的铁栅栏和窗户之间。

爆炸的力量导致关闭的栅栏向外弯曲并震碎了窗户，但未对屋内人员或道路上的行人造成伤害，也未对场所内部造成损害。

在里面工作的三名雇员无法提供有关犯罪原因的信息。

上述隶属于该报社工作人员、案发时站在人行道上的新闻记者也无法提供有关犯罪原因或理由的任何信息，但表示道路上未发生任何引起怀疑的事情。

然而，在霞飞路632弄口执勤的 C.P.V. 975 表示，爆炸发生后，他立即观察到一名身穿长衫的中国男子从现场跑开，进入一辆不明机动车，该车随后向东驶离。

page_data.en:
1/Sheet No. 4.

No substantiation of the above was obtained from
pedestrians interrogated in the near vicinity.

Sub-Inspector Algazin on patrol on Moulmein Road
about fifty yards from the scene, heard the explosion
which he stated sounded like the explosion of a motor
car tyre.

Interrogation of the complainant also failed to
obtain any information that would assist investigations,
but he stated that he suspected the persons responsible
for two similar offences which have recently occurred in
the French Concession, and which complainant alleges to
be "white Russians."

D.S.I. Prokofief and D.S. Lockwood attached to
Special Branch also attended the scene, and upon their
arrival, the complainant produced a slip of writing
paper stated to be a threatening letter, on which was
written in Russian.

"Well, you bloody whore, at last I am in Shanghai,
I intend to get busy about your beautiful mug, one
right to the jaw and one to the left. Take care,
you anarchist whore.
X. P."

Complainant stated that he did not know the origin
of the above letter, and the envelope in which same had
arrived was written in block letters, and had been
destroyed.

The letter was translated by D.S.I. Prokofief, who
page_data.zh:
1/表格编号 4。

在附近讯问的行人未能提供上述情况的任何佐证。

副督察 Algazin（音译）在距现场约五十码的莫尔缅路（Moulmein Road）巡逻时，听到了爆炸声，他称该声音听起来像汽车轮胎爆裂声。

对报案人的讯问也未能获得有助于调查的任何信息，但他表示，他怀疑肇事者与最近在法租界发生的两起类似案件有关，报案人称这些人是“白俄”。

隶属于特务科（Special Branch）的副督察 Prokofief 和警佐 Lockwood 也赶到了现场，他们到达后，报案人出示了一张据称是恐吓信的纸条，上面用俄文写着：

“好吧，你这该死的婊子，我终于到上海了，我打算好好收拾你那张漂亮的脸，一拳打在你下巴右边，一拳打在左边。小心点，你这无政府主义的婊子。
X. P.”

报案人称他不知道上述信件的来源，收到该信的信封是用印刷体字母书写的，且已被销毁。

该信件由副督察 Prokofief 翻译，他

page_data.en:
Sheet No. 5.

now has some in his custody.

It should be stated that complainant when interro-
gated by station staff, refused to admit knowledge of
any threatening letter, but produced this upon interro-
gation by Special Branch representatives, to whom he
is willing to converse, but has a peculiar antipathy
towards dealing direct with the station staff.

Search of the premises resulted in the finding of
numerous small pieces of metal, presumably shrapnel
pieces of the exploded missile, there being of brass
casting and of cheap material.

F. J. Bojko who later attended the scene was
given by inmates a metal spring about three inches in
length, also a double length of wire shaped like a
hook, and from these it could appear that a time bomb
had been hung from the iron grille protecting the
window.

Should this be correct, this would discount the
story of the C.P.W. and substantiate that of the news
reporter, N.A. Schagoleff, employed by the complainant.

Opposite the scene, and on the French Concession
side of Avenue Foch is an Indian named Babu Singh,
employed as a garage watchman, but this man upon being
interrogated with the aid of Station Interpreter S.P.C.
211, could give no information, other than hearing the
page_data.zh:
表格编号 5。

现在保管着该信件的部分内容。

需要说明的是，报案人在接受警局职员讯问时，拒绝承认知晓任何恐吓信，但在接受特务科代表讯问时却出示了此信；他愿意与特务科代表交谈，但对直接与警局职员打交道怀有一种特殊的反感。

对住所的搜查结果发现了大量金属碎片，推测为爆炸弹片的破片，材质包括黄铜铸件和廉价材料。

随后赶到现场的 F. J. Bojko（音译）从住户处获得了一根长约三英寸的金属弹簧，以及一段双股弯成钩状的铁丝，据此看来，定时炸弹似乎是悬挂在保护窗户的铁栅栏上的。

如果情况属实，这将否定中国巡捕（C.P.W.）的说法，并证实受雇于报案人的新闻记者 N.A. Schagoleff（音译）的说法。

在现场对面，福煦路（Avenue Foch）的法租界一侧，有一名名为 Babu Singh 的印度人，受雇为车库看守，但在警局译员 S.P.C. 211 的协助下对其进行讯问时，除了听到

page_data.en:
1/Sheet No. 6.

explosion, and observing a crowd gather.
Nothing unusual was observed by this witness, who
stated that traffic was normal, and no suspicious
characters had been observed in the vicinity prior to
to, or after the offence.
Complainant, V. Sallikin, has come to Police
notice upon numerous occasions and is well known for
his political views, these being of communistic and
anti Japanese nature, and this would give sufficient
reason for the attack.
At the same time, he has antagonised many of the
local Russian community due to his political views and
scathing articles which have from time to time appeared
in the journal under his control, providing another
incentive for intimidation by either personal or political
enemies, and it is no doubt due to this that reason that
the offence was committed.
Further investigations will be conducted regarding
the motive and also the persons responsible for the
offence.
Statements taken from both C.P.U. 975 and the
Indian watchman.
D.O. "F" Div., D.D.O. "A" Div. and Inspector I/c
informed of the occurrence, which was circulated.
D.D.O. "F" Div. attended the scene and conducted
page_data.zh:
1/表格编号 6。

爆炸声并看到人群聚集外，他未能提供任何信息。
这名证人未观察到任何异常情况，他表示交通正常，在案发前或案发后，附近均未发现可疑人物。
报案人 V. Sallikin（音译）已多次引起警方注意，其政治观点为人所知，具有共产主义和反日性质，这构成了袭击的充分理由。
同时，由于其政治观点以及在其控制的刊物上不时发表的尖锐文章，他得罪了许多当地俄国人社区成员，这为个人或政治敌人进行恐吓提供了另一种动机，毫无疑问，正是由于这个原因才实施了此次犯罪。
将进一步调查作案动机及肇事者。
已从中国巡捕 975 号和印度看守处获取供词。
“F”分区警务总监、“A”分区副警务总监及负责督察已获知此事，并已通报各方。

page_data.en:
28/6/4

PoliceContinue
Russian Paper
Bombing Probe

Detectives Believe Job
Work Of Individual,
Not Organization

Detectives of the Chengtu Road
Police station were last night con-
tinuing their investigations of the
mysterious bombing of the Russian
Daily News offices at 620 Avenue
Joffre Wednesday evening but up to
a late hour, they were still attempt-
ing to learn the identity of the for-
eigner who allegedly committed the
bombing and then disappeared.
In the meantime, however, the
paper continued to function as
usual. All reporters and printing
shop hands turned up on time yes-
terday and the fact that front
ground floor offices were damaged
caused no hitch in the normal office
routine.
Detectives last night were in-
clined to accept the theory that
the bombing was the work of some
individual rather than an organiza-
tion. In fact, they believe that
some crack-pot may have been re-
sponsible not only for the bombing
of the newspaper but the placing of
bombs inside the Soviet Trade and
Export offices in the Grosvenor
House and the Soviet Club on Yu
Yuen Road.
In the event that this theory is
correct, a potential killer is at large
and on the loose and until his cap-
ture, similar incidents can be ex-
pected to occur.
The bomb which exploded in the
offices of the Russian Daily News
was a strong, home-made affair that
splintered into more than 60 pieces
of shrapnel when it exploded. The
bomb was touched off by a cotton
fuse and the blast blew out the
front window. Fortunately the
office was empty of workers at the
time and no one was injured.
page_data.zh:
1940年6月28日

警方继续
俄文报纸
爆炸案调查

侦探相信是个别人员所为，
而非组织行为

成都路警局的侦探昨晚继续调查周三晚上发生在福煦路620号《俄罗斯日报》社的神秘爆炸案，但直到很晚，他们仍在试图查明据称实施爆炸随后消失的那名外国人的身份。
与此同时，该报继续照常运作。所有记者和印刷工人都按时上班，底层办公室受损的事实并未影响正常的办公流程。
侦探昨晚倾向于接受这样一种理论，即爆炸案是某个人而非某个组织所为。事实上，他们认为可能是一个疯子不仅对报社实施了爆炸，还在格罗夫纳公寓（Grosvenor House）的苏联贸易出口办事处和愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）的苏联俱乐部内放置了炸弹。
如果这一理论正确，那么一名潜在的杀手正在逍遥法外，在他被抓获之前，预计会发生类似事件。
在《俄罗斯日报》社办公室爆炸的炸弹是一枚威力强大的自制炸弹，爆炸时碎裂成60多块弹片。炸弹由棉引信点燃，爆炸气浪炸飞了前窗。幸运的是，当时办公室内没有工作人员，无人受伤。

The office of the "Russian Daily
News" at 620 Avenue Foch was the
scene of a hand-grenade explosion at
about 7.45 p.m. yesterday. A window
pane at the front door was shattered
and the iron grills were slightly
damaged.
A watchman at the corner of the
street was reported to have seen a
foreigner leaving the place in a motor
car soon after the incident. Police
from Chengtu Road Station were in-
vestigating the case last night.
At the time of the explosion, three
Chinese were on the ground floor
busy with lino-type machines. None
of them was injured.
An official of the paper could give
no reason as to the cause of the
incident.

报社办公室

昨天下午7点45分左右，福煦路620号《俄罗斯日报》社发生手榴弹爆炸。前门的窗玻璃破碎，铁栅栏轻微受损。
据报道，街角的一名看守看到事发后不久有一名外国人乘车离开该地。成都路警局的警察昨晚正在调查此案。
爆炸发生时，三名中国人正在底层忙于操作莱诺铸排机（lino-type machines）。他们均未受伤。
报社的一名官员无法说明事件发生的原因。

page_data.en:
Russian
Journal
Bombed

Hand Grenade Explodes
On Window; Members
Escape Injury

Members of the staff of the Rus-
sian "Daily News," 620 Avenue
Joffre, had a narrow escape from
serious injury last night when at
7.45, a hand grenade exploded after
it had been placed on a window
ledge by an unidentified foreigner,
believed to be a Russian.

Eye-witnesses stated that the man
drove up to the offices of the
newspaper and placed the grenade
on the ledge of a window in the
type-setting department. A few
second after the man had left, the
missile exploded, shattering the
window, but failing to harm any-
one. The mystery man leaped into
his motor car and disappeared.

Police from Chengtu Road were
called to the scene and collected
a number of fragments of the mis-
sible, and late last night were still
investigating the attack, no reason
for which could be advanced by
the victims.
page_data.zh:
俄文
期刊
遭炸

手榴弹在窗户处爆炸；
员工幸免于难

昨晚7点45分，当一名身份不明的外国人（据信是俄国人）将手榴弹放在窗台上后，福煦路620号俄文《每日新闻》社的员工险些受重伤。

目击者称，该男子驾车来到报社办公室，将手榴弹放在排版部一个窗户的窗台上。在该男子离开几秒后，弹药爆炸，震碎了窗户，但未造成任何人受伤。这名神秘男子跳上汽车后消失。

成都路警方被召至现场，收集了一些弹药碎片，昨晚深夜仍在调查此次袭击，受害者无法提出任何作案原因。

page_data.en:
76.99

Political Hooligan—
Blamed For Bombing
Of Russian Daily

A "political hooligan" is blamed
by Mr. V. Chilikin, editor and
publisher of the Russian Daily
News, for the placing of a hand-
grenade on a window sill of the
newspaper premises at 630 Avenue
Foch last night. For the past few
months, he stated, there has been
no trouble with disgruntled read-
ers who objected to the "neutral
policy" of the newspaper.

The grenade, some 200 pieces of
which have been found, is be-
lieved to have been homemade.
Fortunately nobody was in the
machine room at the time of the
explosion, only property damage
being reported. The metal frame
on the window was twisted, the
glass broken and furniture near
the window damaged, the total
loss being placed at $300.

The Settlement Police are in-
vestigating the affair and since
last night an armed guard has
been on duty outside the news-
paper building. No suspects have
as yet been arrested.

Up until about the time of the
hostilities, the editor had re-
ceived threatening telephone
calls and anonymous letters from
people who did not agree with the
political views of editorials, but
no trouble ever resulted. The
paper intends to continue follow-
ing its former policy and will
appear regularly as before.

S. 1
282 9/2
page_data.zh:
76.99

政治流氓——
被指责为
《俄罗斯日报》爆炸案凶手

《俄罗斯日报》编辑兼出版人 V. Chilikin（音译）先生指责一名“政治流氓”昨晚将一枚手榴弹放置在福煦路630号报社 premises 的窗台上。他表示，过去几个月里，那些反对报纸“中立政策”的不满读者并没有制造麻烦。

这枚手榴弹已找到约200块碎片，据信是自制的。幸运的是，爆炸时机房内无人，仅报告有财产损失。窗户的金属框架扭曲，玻璃破碎，窗户附近的家具受损，总损失估计为300美元。

公共租界警方正在调查此事，自昨晚以来，报社大楼外一直有武装警卫执勤。目前尚未逮捕任何嫌疑人。

直到战事爆发前后，编辑曾接到不同意社论政治观点的人打来的恐吓电话和匿名信，但从未引发麻烦。该报打算继续遵循其以往的政策，并将像以前一样定期出版。

S. 1

of the Russian newspaper which had been engaged in anti- 
Jepenese propaganda by an unknown person giv<s a good 
indication of conditions in the Settl-mente

be allowed to be useé as?) base for the anti-Jepenese 
activities. The Settlement is no longer surrounded by 
the Chinese army; the Japamese army Ras saved the 
Settlement from being over-ridden by the Chinese army.

the case of the French Concession which can not be alloved 
to be used as a base for the anti-Jepanese activities,
